data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 claims a synchronized Recovery Wave indicates failures were all awaiting resolution of a single shared external constraint, and that truly independent failures exhibit stochastic recovery times. But its own countercondition supplies the refuting case: a global automated reboot script can synchronize recovery without the original failures sharing a cause. In that scenario, independent local failures recover in a synchronized wave purely due to the shared recovery mechanism, yet SRC_004's mechanism would classify them as correlated-by-cause. The target therefore cannot support 'uniquely identifiable': a synchronized recovery wave is not unique to shared-cause failure once a shared recovery mechanism can produce the identical signature.
